points.place: 爱尔兰沃特福德郡利斯莫尔城堡
points.title: 贵族童年
points.description: 罗伯特·波义耳出生于爱尔兰利斯莫尔城堡的一个富裕贵族家庭，是理查德·波义耳伯爵的第七个儿子。作为家中最小的孩子，他从小接受了良好的教育，但体弱多病。这段时期，他接触到了各种科学书籍，尤其是伽利略和笛卡尔的著作，这为他后来的科学探索奠定了基础。利斯莫尔城堡的图书馆成为他早期学习的重要场所，培养了他对自然哲学的浓厚兴趣。
points.descriptionEn: Robert Boyle was born in Lismore Castle, County Waterford, Ireland, into a wealthy aristocratic family as the seventh son of Richard Boyle, Earl of Cork. As the youngest child, he received an excellent education but suffered from poor health. During this period, he was exposed to various scientific works, particularly those of Galileo and Descartes, which laid the foundation for his later scientific explorations. The library at Lismore Castle became an important place for his early studies, cultivating his deep interest in natural philosophy.

points.place: 欧洲大陆（瑞士、意大利、法国）
points.title: 欧洲游学
points.description: 14岁时，波义耳开始了欧洲大陆的游学之旅，先后在日内瓦、佛罗伦萨和巴黎等地学习。在意大利，他遇到了伽利略的学生卡斯泰利，进一步加深了对实验科学的理解。这段经历使波义耳接触到了欧洲最新的科学思想和实验方法，尤其是伽利略的实验传统。欧洲游学不仅拓宽了他的视野，也确立了他对实验科学的坚定信念，为他日后成为实验科学的先驱奠定了思想基础。
points.descriptionEn: At the age of 14, Boyle began a grand tour of the European continent, studying in Geneva, Florence, and Paris. In Italy, he met Castelli, a student of Galileo, which deepened his understanding of experimental science. This experience exposed Boyle to the latest scientific ideas and experimental methods in Europe, particularly Galileo's experimental tradition. The European tour not only broadened his horizons but also solidified his commitment to experimental science, laying the ideological foundation for his later role as a pioneer of experimental science.

points.title: 牛津实验时期
points.description: 1654年，波义耳移居牛津，加入了新成立的牛津大学实验哲学俱乐部，这个俱乐部后来发展成为皇家学会。在这里，他与罗伯特·胡克合作，改进了真空泵，设计出了著名的波义耳定律实验装置。1662年，他发表了著名的波义耳定律，描述了在恒温条件下，气体的体积与压力成反比的关系。这一时期，波义耳进行了大量关于气体性质、化学反应和燃烧现象的实验，奠定了现代化学和物理学的基础。牛津时期是波义耳科学成就最辉煌的阶段，他的实验方法和科学思想对后世产生了深远影响。
points.descriptionEn: In 1654, Boyle moved to Oxford and joined the newly formed Oxford Experimental Philosophy Club, which later evolved into the Royal Society. Here, he collaborated with Robert Hooke, improving the air pump and designing the famous apparatus for Boyle's law experiments. In 1662, he published his famous law describing the inverse relationship between the volume and pressure of a gas at constant temperature. During this period, Boyle conducted numerous experiments on gas properties, chemical reactions, and combustion phenomena, laying the foundation for modern chemistry and physics. The Oxford period marked the pinnacle of Boyle's scientific achievements, and his experimental methods and scientific ideas had a profound impact on later generations.

points.title: 伦敦著述时期
points.description: 1668年，波义耳移居伦敦，继续他的科学研究并开始系统性地整理和发表他的研究成果。这一时期，他完成了《怀疑的化学家》(The Sceptical Chymist)等重要著作，批判了当时流行的四元素说，提出了元素的科学定义，为现代化学的发展指明了方向。波义耳还积极参与皇家学会的活动，担任了学会的理事。在伦敦，他建立了私人实验室，吸引了众多年轻学者前来学习交流。这一时期，波义耳的科学思想更加成熟，他强调实验验证的重要性，主张科学应该基于可重复的实验观察，而非纯粹的思辨。
points.descriptionEn: In 1668, Boyle moved to London, continuing his scientific research and beginning to systematically organize and publish his findings. During this period, he completed important works such as 'The Sceptical Chymist,' criticizing the prevailing theory of four elements and proposing a scientific definition of elements, pointing the way for the development of modern chemistry. Boyle also actively participated in the activities of the Royal Society, serving as its director. In London, he established a private laboratory that attracted many young scholars for study and exchange. During this time, Boyle's scientific ideas matured further as he emphasized the importance of experimental verification and advocated that science should be based on repeatable experimental observations rather than pure speculation.

points.title: 晚年与遗产
points.description: 1688年后，波义耳的健康状况逐渐恶化，但他仍然坚持科学研究。他将大量财产用于慈善事业，资助翻译圣经，并支持宗教宽容。波义耳终身未婚，他将遗产的一部分用于建立波义耳讲座，旨在向公众传播科学知识。1691年，波义耳在伦敦逝世。作为现代化学的奠基人之一，波义耳的贡献不仅在于他的科学发现，更在于他倡导的实验方法和科学精神。他强调科学应该基于实验证据，而非权威或传统，这一理念对后世科学发展产生了深远影响。波义耳被尊为'现代化学之父'，他的科学思想和实验方法至今仍影响着科学研究的方式。
points.descriptionEn: After 1688, Boyle's health gradually declined, but he continued to engage in scientific research. He donated much of his fortune to charitable causes, supported Bible translation, and advocated for religious tolerance. Boyle never married and used part of his estate to establish the Boyle Lectures aimed at disseminating scientific knowledge to the public. Boyle died in London in 1691. As one of the founders of modern chemistry, Boyle's contributions lie not only in his scientific discoveries but also in the experimental methods and scientific spirit he advocated. He emphasized that science should be based on experimental evidence rather than authority or tradition, an idea that has had a profound impact on the development of science. Boyle is revered as the 'father of modern chemistry,' and his scientific ideas and experimental methods continue to influence the way scientific research is conducted today.

supporter.zh: 波义耳被誉为'现代化学之父'，他的科学贡献不可估量。他通过实验确立了气体定律，为化学和物理学奠定了定量基础。波义耳强调实验验证的重要性，主张科学应该基于可重复的观察，而非纯粹的思辨，这一理念彻底改变了科学研究的方法。他的《怀疑的化学家》批判了四元素说，提出了元素的科学定义，为现代化学的发展指明了方向。波义耳还积极参与皇家学会的建立，推动了科学共同体的形成，他的科学精神和实验方法至今仍影响着科学研究的方式。
supporter.en: Boyle is hailed as the 'father of modern chemistry' for his immeasurable scientific contributions. He established gas laws through experiments, laying the quantitative foundation for chemistry and physics. Boyle emphasized the importance of experimental verification and advocated that science should be based on repeatable observations rather than pure speculation, an approach that revolutionized scientific methodology. His 'The Sceptical Chymist' criticized the theory of four elements and proposed a scientific definition of elements, pointing the way for modern chemistry. Boyle also actively participated in the establishment of the Royal Society, promoting the formation of scientific communities, and his scientific spirit and experimental methods continue to influence scientific research today.

critic.zh: 尽管波义耳的科学贡献巨大，但他也存在明显的局限性。他未能完全摆脱炼金术的影响，在解释化学反应时仍带有神秘主义色彩。波义耳的实验方法虽然开创性，但缺乏系统性和精确性，许多实验结果难以重复。此外，他作为贵族，其科学活动主要依靠个人财富支持，这种模式限制了科学研究的普及和系统性发展。波义耳还未能完全摆脱宗教思想的束缚，他的科学著作中常常融合神学观点，这在一定程度上限制了他对自然现象的客观解释。
critic.en: Despite Boyle's immense scientific contributions, he had clear limitations. He failed to completely摆脱 the influence of alchemy, explaining chemical reactions with mystical elements. Boyle's experimental methods, though pioneering, lacked systematic precision, making many experimental results difficult to replicate. Additionally, as an aristocrat, his scientific activities relied primarily on personal wealth, a model that limited the popularization and systematic development of scientific research. Boyle also could not completely free himself from religious constraints, often integrating theological views in his scientific works, which to some extent limited his objective explanations of natural phenomena.

objective.zh: 在历史学界，波义耳被定位为科学革命的关键人物，他代表了从传统自然哲学向现代实验科学的转变。他的科学思想和实验方法对皇家学会的发展产生了深远影响，塑造了早期现代科学的研究范式。在流行文化中，波义耳常被描绘为理性与实验精神的象征，他的名字与波义耳定律一起成为科学教育的经典内容。波义耳的科学遗产不仅在于他的具体发现，更在于他倡导的科学方法和科学精神，这种强调实验验证和批判性思考的理念至今仍是科学研究的核心价值。
objective.en: In historical scholarship, Boyle is positioned as a key figure in the Scientific Revolution, representing the transition from traditional natural philosophy to modern experimental science. His scientific ideas and experimental methods profoundly influenced the development of the Royal Society, shaping the research paradigm of early modern science. In popular culture, Boyle is often depicted as a symbol of reason and experimental spirit, with his name and Boyle's law becoming classic content in science education. Boyle's scientific legacy lies not only in his specific discoveries but in the scientific methods and spirit he advocated—an emphasis on experimental verification and critical thinking that remains central to scientific research today.

self.zh: 我所做的实验不是为了满足好奇心，而是为了发现自然的规律。
self.en: The experiments I make are not for the sake of amusing myself, but for the sake of discovering the nature of things.

others.zh: 波义耳是实验哲学的真正创始人，他通过实验而非权威来探索自然。
others.en: Boyle was the true founder of experimental philosophy, who explored nature through experiments rather than authority.
